title: N+1 query diagnosis
description: Learn to identify and fix N+1 query problems in EF Core, one of the most common and damaging performance anti-patterns in data-access code.

data.text: The N+1 query problem is one of the most common performance issues in ORM-based applications. It happens when you load a collection of entities and then make a separate database query for each related entity. What should be two queries becomes N+1 — one to load the parent rows and one per parent to load its children.

Imagine loading 100 blog posts and then accessing the `Author` navigation property on each one. If that navigation property is lazy-loaded, EF Core fires 100 individual SELECT statements — one for each post's author. The database connection round-trips and query planning overhead dominate the response time, even though the data is small.

data.title: N+1 problem with lazy loading
How to detect N+1
data.text: Enable EF Core's built-in logging with `LogTo(Console.WriteLine)` or use a tool like MiniProfiler. If you see repeated queries inside a loop — especially queries on related tables — you are likely looking at N+1. Application Performance Monitoring (APM) tools also surface repeated identical queries.

items: Lazy-loading proxies enabled on navigation properties that are accessed inside a loop.
Serializing tracked entities with navigation properties — the serializer touches each property, triggering lazy loads.
Mixing `Include` with projection: `Include` loads full entities, then a `Select` accesses a navigation property that was not included.
Iterating over a parent list and accessing a reference navigation property without eager-loading it.

data.text: The most direct fix is to eager-load the related data using `Include` before you iterate. This consolidates all data retrieval into a single query. For reference navigations (many-to-one), this is usually the cleanest solution.

data.title: Fixing N+1 with eager loading

data.text: For read-only scenarios, projection is often better than Include. By selecting exactly the fields you need into a DTO, EF Core generates a single, efficient SQL query with no tracking overhead and no risk of lazy-loading side effects.

data.title: Fixing N+1 with projection

data.text: Returning tracked entities directly from API endpoints is risky. JSON serializers like System.Text.Json traverse every property by default, including navigation properties. If lazy-loading is enabled, serialization silently triggers N+1 queries. Use DTOs with projection to control exactly what gets serialized and fetched.

data.title: Key takeaways
items: N+1 occurs when a collection query is followed by individual queries per item.
Lazy loading and serialization of tracked entities are common causes.
Use Include or projection to load related data in a single round-trip.
Enable EF Core logging to spot repeated queries during development.
